extDescription.message: Redirect, modify, block and mock HTTP requests, plus a lightweight API client. No servers, accounts or telemetry.
extDescription.description: Store and extensions page description. At most 132 characters.

popupTagline.message: Redirect, change and block requests. Everything stays in your browser.

navLabel.description: Accessible name of the sidebar navigation.

policyDescription.message: Settings that your organization's administrator sets through the browser's policy. They take precedence over yours, and you can't change them here.

policyEmptyText.message: Every feature is available, and only you decide how InterceptKit works.

policyIssues.message: The policy has errors. A broken restriction is read in its strictest form, and other broken values are ignored.

policyPresetBundle.message: Rules and mocks of the organization

policyNoHosts.message: None: InterceptKit can't get access to any site

policyUserRulesForbidden.message: Don't apply: only those of the organization do

policyPresetBroken.message: Don't apply: the bundle has errors

transferDescription.message: Move rules, mocks and environments between browsers and people as a JSON file that is easy to keep in git.

transferExportHint.message: Records of the organization policy and the values of secrets never go into the file: secret variables keep their names, empty.

transferImportHint.message: A record with a known id replaces the one stored here, and nothing is deleted. Secret values this browser keeps stay, and records of the policy are never touched.

transferImportText.message: Or paste the text of a file

transferFileUnreadable.message: The file could not be read.

transferCounts.message: $1 — new: $2, replaced: $3, kept from the policy: $4
transferCounts.description: $1 is a list such as Rules; $2, $3 and $4 are numbers.

transferImportFailed.message: The import did not go through: $1
transferImportFailed.description: $1 is the technical reason, in English.

interceptionOn.message: Enabled rules and mocks work on allowed sites.

interceptionOff.message: Paused: no rule or mock applies.

interceptionPaused.message: Interception is paused, so none of these rules apply right now.

rulesDescription.message: Redirect requests, change their headers or block them. If several rules match a request, the one higher in the list wins.

rulesNoSites.message: Rules only work on sites you allow, and you haven't allowed any yet.

rulesPolicyOnly.message: Your organization allows only its own rules, so the rules you add don't apply.

rulesFeaturesOff.message: Your organization turned off: $1. Rules of these types don't apply.
rulesFeaturesOff.description: $1 is a list of features, such as Redirects, Blocking.

rulesEmptyText.message: A rule picks requests by their URL and redirects them, changes their headers or blocks them.

rulesActionFailed.message: Couldn't update the rule. Try again.

ruleNoAccess.message: InterceptKit has no access to $1, so the rule doesn't work there yet.
ruleNoAccess.description: $1 is a host name, such as api.example.com.

ruleHostNotAllowed.message: Your organization doesn't allow access to $1, so the rule doesn't work there.
ruleHostNotAllowed.description: $1 is a host name, such as api.example.com.

ruleBadgeRedirect.description: Short name of the action in the rule list.

ruleBadgeHeaders.description: Short name of the action in the rule list.

ruleBadgeBlock.description: Short name of the action in the rule list.

ruleSummaryRedirect.description: $1 is the redirect target, such as a URL.

ruleSummaryTransform.description: $1 lists the changed parts, such as Port: 8080.

ruleSummaryHeaders.description: $1 lists header names, such as X-Debug, Cookie.

rulesSaveFailed.description: $1 is the technical reason, in English.

rulesDeleteText.message: The rule “$1” will be deleted. This can't be undone.

ruleTypeRedirectHint.message: Sends matching requests to another URL.

ruleTypeHeadersHint.message: Sets, appends or removes headers of matching requests and their responses.

ruleTypeBlockHint.message: Matching requests never reach the network and fail with an error.

rulePatternFilterHint.message: || anchors a domain, * matches any characters and ^ matches a separator such as / or ?.

rulePatternRegexHint.message: RE2 syntax, as in Chrome. Groups in parentheses can be reused in a redirect.

ruleMethodsHint.message: Select none to match any method.

ruleResourceTypesHint.message: Select none to match every type, page loads included.

ruleInitiatorDomainsHint.message: Separate domains with commas. Their subdomains are included.

ruleSubstitutionHint.message: \1 to \9 insert the groups captured by the regular expression.

ruleSubstitutionNeedsRegex.message: A substitution needs groups from a regular expression. Switch the pattern type above to Regular expression.

ruleTransformHint.message: Leave a field empty to keep that part of the original URL.

ruleHeaderDelete.description: Accessible name of the × button in a header row.

sitesDescription.message: InterceptKit works only on sites you allow. The browser checks access to both the site a request goes to and the page that sends it. Mocks answer only on sites where you turn them on.

sitesDomainPlaceholder.description: Sample domain in an empty input. Not translated.

sitesEmptyText.message: Enter a domain above. The browser will ask you to confirm access.

sitesWithSubdomains.description: Badge next to a domain whose subdomains are allowed too.

sitesInvalidDomain.message: Enter a domain, for example example.com or localhost.

sitesNotAllowed.message: Your organization doesn't allow access to this site.

sitesSubdomainsNotAllowed.message: Your organization allows this site without its subdomains: turn off Include subdomains.

sitesAllowedHosts.message: Your organization allows access only to these sites: $1.
sitesAllowedHosts.description: $1 is a list of hosts, such as example.com, *.example.org.

sitesNoHostsAllowed.message: Your organization doesn't allow access to any site.

sitesMocksFailed.message: Couldn't switch mocks for the site. Try again.

mocksDescription.message: Answer the page's fetch and XHR requests with your own responses. If several mocks match a request, the one higher in the list answers. Open pages get changes after a reload.

mocksPaused.message: Interception is paused, so mocks don't answer right now.

mocksNoSites.message: Mocks work only on sites where you turn them on, and no site has them on yet.

mocksPolicyOnly.message: Your organization allows only its own mocks, so the mocks you add don't apply.

mocksFeatureOff.message: Your organization turned off the Mock API, so no mock applies.

mocksSecretsWarning.message: Scripts of the page can read its mocks, so don't put tokens, passwords or other secrets into them.

mocksEmptyText.message: A mock finds requests by URL and answers them with the status, headers and body you set.

mocksActionFailed.message: Couldn't update the mock. Try again.

mocksSaveFailed.description: $1 is the technical reason, in English.

mocksDeleteText.message: The mock “$1” will be deleted. This can't be undone.

mockSummaryMethods.description: $1 is a list of HTTP methods.

mockDelayHint.message: Up to 60,000 ms. Leave empty to answer at once.

mockBodyHint.message: A JSON body must be valid JSON. Statuses such as 204 take no body.

mockHeadersEmpty.message: Without headers the response gets only a content type for its body format.

settingsDescription.message: How InterceptKit looks in this browser.

languageEnglish.description: Language name in that language. Not translated.

languageRussian.description: Language name in that language. Not translated.

settingsPrivacy.message: Rules and settings are stored only in this browser. InterceptKit has no servers, accounts or telemetry.

settingsSaveFailed.message: Couldn't save the setting. Try again.

apiClientDisabledTitle.message: Your organization turned the API client off

apiClientDisabledText.message: Your organization's administrator turned it off through the browser's policy. The history of requests stays where it was.

apiClientNewTab.description: Title of a request tab while its URL is empty.

apiClientTabClose.description: $1 is the title of the tab: a URL or “New request”.

apiClientParamsEmpty.message: Parameters go into the query after the URL, next to the ones it already has.

apiClientHeadersEmpty.message: The browser adds headers of its own, such as Accept and User-Agent.

apiClientRuleHeaders.message: fetch() cannot send these headers, so a browser rule sets them on this request only: $1. A Cookie header replaces the site's cookies.
apiClientRuleHeaders.description: $1 is a comma-separated list of header names.

apiClientBrowserHeaders.message: The browser builds these headers itself, so the values typed here aren't sent: $1.
apiClientBrowserHeaders.description: $1 is a comma-separated list of header names.

apiClientBodyNoneHint.message: The request goes without a body.

apiClientContentTypeHint.message: Goes as the Content-Type header unless the headers set one.

apiClientBodyless.message: $1 requests go without a body. It's kept here for another method.

apiClientSendCookiesHint.message: Off: the request goes without your cookies for the site. On: the browser adds all of them, including the cookies of the session you're signed in with.

apiClientResponseIdle.message: Send the request, and its response shows up here.

apiClientResponseBinary.message: The body isn't text ($1), so it isn't shown.
apiClientResponseBinary.description: $1 is the content type, such as image/png.

apiClientResponseCookiesNote.message: Set-Cookie isn't listed: the browser hides it from pages.

apiClientInvalidRequest.description: $1 is the technical reason, in English.

apiClientSendFailed.description: $1 is what the browser reported, in English.

apiClientTimedOut.message: The whole response did not come back within $1 seconds, so the request was given up.

apiClientResponseTruncated.message: The response is larger than $1, so only its beginning was downloaded.
apiClientResponseTruncated.description: $1 is a size such as 10 MB.

apiClientSendFailedHint.message: The server may be down or out of reach, or the browser may not trust its certificate.

apiClientNoAccess.message: InterceptKit has no access to $1, and without it the browser would hide the response.

apiClientHostNotAllowed.message: Your organization doesn't allow requests to $1.

apiClientHistoryHint.message: Requests you send show up here, the last $1 of them. They are kept as typed, with {{variables}} but without their values.
apiClientHistoryHint.description: $1 is the number of requests the history keeps.

apiClientHistoryClearText.message: Every request in the history will be deleted. Open tabs stay as they are.

apiClientHistoryActionFailed.message: Couldn't change the history. Try again.

apiClientMissingVariables.message: No value for $1: choose an environment that has these variables, or add them to it.
apiClientMissingVariables.description: $1 is a comma-separated list of variable names.

apiClientEnvironmentsEmpty.message: An environment keeps values such as {{baseUrl}} or {{token}} for one stage. Choose the environment at the top of the page.

apiClientEnvironmentEditNamed.description: $1 is the name of an environment.

apiClientEnvironmentDeleteNamed.description: $1 is the name of an environment.

apiClientEnvironmentsActionFailed.message: Couldn't change the environments. Try again.

apiClientEnvironmentSaveFailed.description: $1 is the technical reason, in English.

apiClientEnvironmentDeleteText.message: The environment “$1” and its variables will be deleted. This can't be undone.

apiClientVariablesHint.message: A request uses a variable as {{name}}: in the URL, parameters, headers and body.

apiClientSecretsWarning.message: Secret values are hidden on the screen, but this browser's profile keeps them unencrypted. To encrypt them with a master password, use the button at the top of the page.

apiClientVaultRequiredWarning.message: Your organization requires secrets to be encrypted: values of variables marked Secret aren't saved until you turn on encryption.

apiClientSecretsEncrypted.message: Secret values are encrypted with the master password. The editor never shows them: type a new value to replace one.

apiClientSecretsLocked.message: The vault is locked, so these encrypted variables have no value: $1. Unlock it at the top of the page.
apiClientSecretsLocked.description: $1 is a comma-separated list of variable names.

apiClientVaultRequired.message: Your organization requires secrets to be encrypted: turn on encryption to use $1.
apiClientVaultRequired.description: $1 is a list of variable names.

apiClientVaultChangeText.message: Secret values are encrypted again with a key from the new password.

apiClientVaultFailed.message: The vault did not respond. Try again.

apiClientVaultSetupText.message: Secret values of every environment are encrypted with a key derived from the master password. The password itself is stored nowhere.

apiClientVaultSetupWarning.message: If you forget the password, the encrypted values cannot be recovered: you can only reset the vault and type them again.

apiClientVaultAutoLockHint.message: The vault locks itself after $1 minutes without use and when the browser closes.

apiClientVaultUnlockText.message: Enter the master password to put encrypted values into requests.

apiClientVaultDisableText.message: Secret values are decrypted and kept in this browser's profile unencrypted again. Enter the master password to confirm.

apiClientVaultResetText.message: The encrypted values are deleted and encryption turns off. The variables stay, but empty: type their values again.

apiClientVaultLockedSave.message: The vault is locked: unlock it at the top of the page to save secret values.

apiClientVaultRequiredSave.message: Your organization requires secrets to be encrypted. Turn on encryption, then save again.

apiClientCurlCommandHint.message: For example, from “Copy as cURL (bash)” in the browser's developer tools. The request opens in a new tab. Commands for cmd and PowerShell are not supported.

apiClientCurlCommandPlaceholder.description: An example command; keep it as is.

apiClientCurlImportFailed.description: $1 is the technical reason, in English.

apiClientCurlExportSecretsHint.message: Without it, secrets stay as {{name}}, so a token doesn't end up in the clipboard.

apiClientCurlExportMissing.message: These variables have no value and stay as typed: $1.
apiClientCurlExportMissing.description: $1 is a comma-separated list of variable names.

apiClientCurlExportCookies.message: The browser's cookies for the site are not in the command: add a Cookie header if the server needs them.

apiClientCurlExportCopyFailed.message: Couldn't copy: select the command and copy it yourself.

apiClientCollectionsEmpty.message: Keep requests in collections and folders. Save the request of a tab with Ctrl+S.

apiClientCollectionsLimit.message: There can be at most $1 collections.

apiClientCollectionMenu.description: $1 is the name of a collection, a folder or a request.

apiClientCollectionDeleteText.message: “$1” will be deleted, with everything inside if it is a folder or a collection. Open tabs keep their requests.
apiClientCollectionDeleteText.description: $1 is the name of a collection, a folder or a request.

apiClientImportHint.message: A Postman collection (v2.0 or v2.1) or environment, or an OpenAPI 3.0 or 3.1 description, as JSON. Up to 10 MB.

apiClientImportText.message: Or paste the text of a file

apiClientImportFileUnreadable.message: The file could not be read.

apiClientImportCollection.description: $1 is a name, $2 and $3 are numbers.

apiClientImportEnvironment.message: A new environment “$1”: variables: $2. Choose it at the top of the page to use them.
apiClientImportEnvironment.description: $1 is a name, $2 is a number.

apiClientImportSecretsPlain.message: Secret values will be stored unencrypted, as if typed in the editor. To encrypt them, turn on encryption at the top of the page before the import.

apiClientImportSecretsEncrypted.message: Secret values will be encrypted with the master password.

apiClientImportSecretsLocked.message: The vault is locked, so secret values will be left empty. To import them, unlock the vault at the top of the page and import the file again.

apiClientImportSecretsRequired.message: Your organization requires secrets to be encrypted, so secret values will be left empty. To import them, turn on encryption and import the file again.

apiClientImportEnvironmentsLimit.message: There can be at most $1 environments.

apiClientImportGapScripts.message: Scripts and tests (scripts: $2): code from a file never runs here

apiClientImportGapBodies.message: Bodies of the kinds $1 (requests: $2): the client sends JSON, text and URL-encoded forms only
apiClientImportGapBodies.description: $1 is a list of body modes, $2 is a number.

apiClientImportGapBodiesOfBodyless.message: Bodies of $1 requests (requests: $2): requests with these methods go without a body
apiClientImportGapBodiesOfBodyless.description: $1 is a list of methods, $2 is a number.

apiClientImportGapAuths.description: $1 is a list of authorization types, $2 is a number.

apiClientImportGapBasicWithVariables.message: Basic authorization with {{variables}} (requests: $2): the header holds the credentials encoded, so a variable inside cannot be filled

apiClientImportGapMethods.message: Requests with the methods $1 (requests: $2): the client does not send them
apiClientImportGapMethods.description: $1 is a list of methods, $2 is a number.

apiClientImportGapDynamicVariables.message: Generated values $1 (requests: $2): they stay as typed, the client does not make them up
apiClientImportGapDynamicVariables.description: $1 is a list of templates, $2 is a number.

apiClientImportGapDeepFolders.message: Folders deeper than five levels (folders: $2): their requests go to the folder of the fifth level

apiClientImportGapVariableNames.message: Variables with names that {{templates}} cannot use: $1

apiClientImportEmptySecrets.message: Fill in these secrets in the environment before sending: $1.

apiClientImportGapRelativeServer.message: The server address $1 is not a full URL: put the address of the API into baseUrl of the environment

apiClientImportGapExternalRefs.message: References to other files $1 (references: $2): only references inside the file are followed
apiClientImportGapExternalRefs.description: $1 is a list of references, $2 is a number.

apiClientImportGapCookieParameters.description: $1 is a list of names, $2 is a number.

apiClientImportGapOwnServers.message: Operations with servers of their own (requests: $2): they go to baseUrl like the others

apiClientImportVariablesSuffix.description: Ends the name of the environment made of the variables of a collection.

dialogClose.description: Accessible name of the button that closes a dialog.

codeEditorFormat.description: Button under a JSON editor that lays the JSON out with indents.
